$comment: MCP tool contract for `check`. The verdict comes only from deterministic engine execution; the model classifies checkability and translates - it never decides. formal_form and engine_result make every verdict auditable (FR-007). not_checkable is a successful, honest outcome (FR-004).
name: check
description: Settle a checkable claim by execution, not judgment. The claim is translated into a small formal problem - an arithmetic comparison or a logic/constraint system - and a deterministic engine executes it: no judge to fool, no calibration, no sycophancy. Returns the verdict with the executed formal form and the engine's raw result so the check is auditable, plus a solver witness when one exists. A claim that bundles several statements is checked part by part: parts holds each part's own verdict, form and result, and the top-level verdict of a bundle is refuted if any part is refuted and not_checkable otherwise - never supported, because nothing can confirm the parts cover every statement of the claim; read each part's verdict in parts. Claims that cannot be formalized honestly (judgment, taste, open questions) return not_checkable with the reason - route those to verify instead.

claim.description: The claim to check, in natural language. Best for arithmetic, quantitative comparisons, and logical/constraint consistency.

context.description: Optional background the claim depends on (definitions, given values).

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this call alone. Omit to use the deployment's configured level. Not every model family accepts this; when one rejects it the error names the model, the level, and the remedies.

engine.description: Which engine executed the check. For a single claim: null iff not_checkable. For a bundle of two or more parts: set only when every part ran on the same engine, so it can be null beside any verdict; read each part's engine in parts.

formal_form.description: The executed expression or constraint script - audit the translation without re-running it. For a bundle of two or more parts: one '[n] form' line per part in part order, '(not checked)' for a part no engine ran, a script collapsed onto its line; null when no part ran. The exact forms are in parts.

engine_result.description: The engine's raw result (evaluated value, or sat/unsat). For a bundle: one '[n] result' line per part, '(not checked)' for a part no engine ran; null when no part ran.

witness.description: Solver model when one exists: the satisfying assignment, or the counterexample refuting an impossibility claim. For a bundle: one '[n] witness' line for each part that has one, collapsed onto its line; null when no part has one.

explanation.description: Deterministic, server-assembled explanation tying the engine result to the claim.

reason.description: Why the claim is not checkable (verdict = not_checkable only). For a bundle whose top-level verdict is not_checkable: first a sentence saying nothing can confirm the parts cover every statement of the claim, then one '[n] reason' line for each part that was not checked.

parts.description: One entry per separately checked part, in the order the claim states them. A single claim has exactly one part. For a bundle of two or more parts the top-level formal_form, engine_result, witness and reason are summaries in '[n] ...' lines as each field describes, engine is set only when every part ran on the same engine, and the top-level verdict of a bundle is refuted if any part is refuted and not_checkable otherwise - never supported - so which parts held is visible only here.

claim.description: The part, restated by the translator so it stands alone.

engine.description: Which engine executed this part; null iff it was not checked.

formal_form.description: The exact expression or constraint script executed for this part.

engine_result.description: The engine's raw result for this part.

witness.description: Solver model for this part, when one exists.

reason.description: Why this part is not checkable (verdict = not_checkable only).
